cards.title: Response-Time Plotting and Baseline Reference Integrity
cards.claim: Response-time plots must preserve record-level integrity, distinguishing individual paired baselines from group-level contrasts and concurrent controls. Display conventions must separate observed points from summaries and handle missing/censored data without substitution.
conditions: Applicable to general PK/PD EDA where response is plotted against time.
Requires documented time origin (e.g., dose or treatment start) and explicit response units.
Individual change calculations require verified individual pairing; group-level contrasts require complete compatible inputs.
BLQ and above-range values must be handled as categorical statuses, not numeric substitutions.
required_inputs: Conditional input mapping: numeric values only for quantified records; optional summaries/errors only when shown; assay-specific or branch-specific fields only when applicable. Missing fields limit dependent operations, not all displays.
Record/source locator, study, design, observation ID.
Experimental-unit ID (nullable), specimen/pool ID, technical-repeat ID.
Regimen, dose occasion, route/formulation, analyte, matrix, free/total basis.
Time value, unit, and origin; measured value, unit, and quantification status.
Documented baseline or reference definitions for change calculations.
Nullable serial_observation_subject_id, distinct from experimental_unit_id (e.g. an animal within its randomized cage); required for individual serial lines or paired loops.
limitations: Response-time shape alone is descriptive and does not identify mechanism (e.g., turnover, effect-site delay) or clinical efficacy.
Unknown serial-subject IDs block individual connections; unknown experimental-unit IDs block independent-unit n/uncertainty, not otherwise verified observed subject series.
Unknown limits block numeric boundary placement but not status display.
This is an engineering display contract, not a regulator-mandated layout or scientific law.
cards.downstream_use: Guides the construction of EDA figures for response-time data, ensuring that visual representations accurately reflect data structure, unit integrity, and quantification limits without implying unsupported mechanistic or statistical conclusions.

plot_recipe.input_contract: Preserve record/source locator, study, design, observation ID, experimental-unit ID (nullable), specimen/pool ID, technical-repeat ID, regimen and dose occasion, route/formulation, analyte, matrix, free/total basis, time value/unit/origin, measured value/unit and quantification status. Map only available applicable fields; never invent missing identities. Preserve nullable serial_observation_subject_id separately from experimental_unit_id, with its source linkage. Numeric measured value is required only for quantified records; censoring/missing statuses may have a null numeric value. Optional summary/error inputs are needed only when that layer is displayed.
plot_recipe.plot_type: Observed response versus documented time, with serial-unit lines only when verified; cross-sectional/destructive points otherwise.
plot_recipe.axes_and_units: X = time with explicit origin (e.g. dose or treatment start); Y = the exact response and unit, or explicitly defined change from a named reference. Show treatment start/stop and relevant events if known. Separate endpoints, assays, matrices and reference definitions.
plot_recipe.grouping_and_connections: Separate study, regimen/dose occasion, route/formulation, analyte/matrix/basis and endpoint contexts. Connect only verified serial observations of the same unit in a compatible time reference, ordered by time. Break connections at recorded unresolved missing/censored statuses. No invented scheduled samples or cross-unit lines. Serial-observation subject ID is distinct from experimental-unit ID: a cage/litter may contain several animals. Individual trajectories or paired loops require the same verified serial_observation_subject_id within study and compatible regimen/time/assay context. A shared cage/litter ID alone never authorizes connecting animals. Unknown serial identity blocks individual lines/pairs, not record-level displays; unknown experimental-unit identity blocks independent-unit n/uncertainty, not an otherwise verified observed subject series.
plot_recipe.point_and_summary_layers: Preserve observed values as points at their actual record level. Keep raw observations separate from optional source-reported or explicitly defined descriptive summaries. A labelled group-summary guide is not an individual trajectory. Do not reconstruct individuals from a mean and SD.
plot_recipe.censoring_and_missingness: The plotted variable is response Y, with its actual endpoint, unit and reference. For a confirmed quantifiable-range censor, use Y<its applicable lower limit or Y>its applicable upper limit only when that assay meaning is established. Microbial count detection/quantification limits, bioanalytical limits and response-scale bounds are distinct. Keep unavailable-after-death, missing, not sampled and technical failure separate from censoring; never invent a zero or apply a concentration LLOQ to response Y.
plot_recipe.transformations_and_formula: Individual change = individual endpoint minus that individual's documented baseline, only with verified pairing. An established group endpoint minus group treatment-start reference is allowed with complete compatible inputs but must be labelled group-level. Endpoint minus concurrent untreated-control response is a different contrast, never relabelled treatment-start baseline. Log transforms require valid positive quantified inputs and a stated reference-unit definition.
plot_recipe.uncertainty_and_n: Label displayed record counts separately from known independent experimental-unit n. Preserve supplied statistic, calculation scale and exact SD, SE or CI meaning, including asymmetric interval endpoints. Technical repeats do not increase biological n. Unknown n or variability stays unknown; no automatic CI or zero-width bar.
plot_recipe.interpretation_limits: Response-time shape alone is not a concentration-response hysteresis loop and does not identify turnover, effect-site delay or clinical benefit. Keep unavailable-after-death or assay-censored outcomes as stated statuses; never create zero responses.
plot_recipe.stop_or_fallback: Block only the operation that needs an unresolved input. Unknown serial-subject IDs block individual connections; unknown experimental-unit IDs block independent-unit summaries. Neither blocks labelled observed record/group displays. Unknown limits block numeric boundary placement, not status display. Unknown time origin permits a source timestamp only if documented; otherwise use a record table. Missing validation documentation means qualification unestablished, not automatically invalid. Serial-observation subject ID is distinct from experimental-unit ID: a cage/litter may contain several animals. Individual trajectories or paired loops require the same verified serial_observation_subject_id within study and compatible regimen/time/assay context. A shared cage/litter ID alone never authorizes connecting animals. Unknown serial identity blocks individual lines/pairs, not record-level displays; unknown experimental-unit identity blocks independent-unit n/uncertainty, not an otherwise verified observed subject series.
plot_recipe.implementation_conventions: This recipe is an explicitly reviewed engineering display contract, not a regulator-mandated layout or scientific law. Use readable legends, separate aligned panels and visible status/count annotations. No universal numeric completeness threshold. No change to source data or current project Rules.

claim_support.claim: ARRIVE asks for summary/descriptive statistics by experimental group, variability where applicable, and exact experimental-unit counts. SD describes dispersion and is not interchangeable with SE or a CI.
claim_support.scope: Animal reporting guidelines for descriptive statistics and experimental unit definition.

claim_support.claim: The FDA guidance discusses assessing response time courses and exposure-response over time to investigate time-related effects. It states that plasma concentration is more directly related to target-site concentration than administered dose alone; this does not identify a mechanism from a response-time plot.
claim_support.scope: General exposure-response guidance on time-dependent responses and concentration-response relationships.

claim_support.claim: The most appropriate representation of exposure depends on study objectives and the nature of the exposure-response relationship; simplified metrics (AUC, Cmax) may be appropriate for single daily responses, while sequential concentration-time data is preferred for time-varying responses.
claim_support.scope: General guidance on selecting exposure metrics based on response time-dependence.
